analysis:
Both changed files are test-only Swift sources under provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests. The change adds a `.logprobs` case to exhaustive switches over MLXServerGenerationEvent: QwenJSONAnswerServingTests.swift line 107 (head) ignores it via `break`, and NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests.swift line 37 (head) maps it to the trace marker "L". This is evidently an adaptation to a new upstream enum case, with no production code in this batch.

I found no change to production trust boundaries, key handling, attestation, the prefix cache (T-041), encryption or authorization. The test helpers never decrypt, persist or transmit anything, so no threat-model asset (A-001 etc.) is touched. The `.logprobs` handling in the Qwen helper deliberately drops the events. The Qwen tests assert content and reasoning only, so a logprobs channel leaking content would not be detected there. That is a test-coverage observation, not a security regression.

The production-side logprobs event is not in the supplied evidence. This covers its emission path and any plaintext exposure through logprobs over the coordinator leg, including the encryption/fail-closed behavior in T-008. The next pass should check that the new `.logprobs` event is sealed like other chunks. NemotronSuperLocalOutputTests line 183 onward already tests logprob carrying for complete responses. Nothing supplied here lets me conclude that production is unsafe, so this stays an unverified contract rather than a finding.
